Workspace join/create, fill, memory sizing, and topology summary logging utilities.

# Purpose
This C file implements the runtime support for a topology object named `fd_topo_t`. It provides functions to join and leave shared-memory workspaces, create workspaces, and map topology objects into local addresses with [`fd_topo_obj_laddr`](<#fd_topo_obj_laddr>). It also fills topology structures with joined handles for links, metrics, and sequence counters, and it calls object-specific creation callbacks through [`fd_topo_wksp_new`](<#fd_topo_wksp_new>). These functions connect the abstract topology description to the shared-memory regions that hold the actual data used by the application.

The file also computes memory and page requirements for the topology. Functions such as [`fd_topo_mlock_max_tile`](<#fd_topo_mlock_max_tile>), [`fd_topo_gigantic_page_cnt`](<#fd_topo_gigantic_page_cnt>), [`fd_topo_huge_page_cnt`](<#fd_topo_huge_page_cnt>), [`fd_topo_normal_page_cnt`](<#fd_topo_normal_page_cnt>), and [`fd_topo_mlock`](<#fd_topo_mlock>) calculate the amount of locked memory and the number of pages needed per NUMA node and per tile. The [`fd_topo_print_log`](<#fd_topo_print_log>) function formats this information into a log summary that lists workspaces, objects, links, and tiles, including their sizes, affinities, and properties.
